tasks.short: Teach writing classes, hold one-to-one writing conferences on drafts, prepare in-class writing exercises, and answer students' questions about assignments.

steps.what: Lecturer teaches writing or communication classes
Lecturer holds writing conferences on students' drafts
Lecturer answers students' questions about writing assignments by e-mail

tasks.design: Before a conference, students run their draft through the formative feedback tool in the learning system ({LMS}), which comments on citation style and set structure criteria the lecturer has chosen, so conferences cover argument and voice instead of formatting. Writing exercises are kept in a shared exercise bank in the learning system and reused across groups. Common assignment questions go on a course FAQ page and forum. Teaching classes stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conferences spent time on citation and format errors, and the same questions came by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems give formative feedback on set writing criteria.
tasks.still_hard: Students who skip the feedback tool still bring format errors.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student find what they really want to say.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer spends conference time on ideas instead of formatting.

evidence.claim: FeedbackFruits Automated Feedback gives formative feedback in the learning system on writing criteria such as citation style; teachers edit the criteria.
AI literacy duties cover all staff who use AI tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the class scheduled to questions answered; grading is outside.
Input contract: feedback tool licensed; fallback is conferences as now.
Students spend a little time running the feedback tool; priced as customer time.
research_questions: Do conferences get shorter or deeper?

incremental.description: Lecturer sets the feedback criteria for each assignment.
Students run their drafts through the feedback tool.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few conferences; high: large groups with many drafts.

tasks.short: Read papers, check length, citation format and references, write feedback comments, decide the grade, and enter grades in the learning and student records systems.

steps.what: Lecturer reads students' papers and assignments
Lecturer checks length, citation format and references by hand
Lecturer writes feedback comments to evaluate class work

loop.input: The paper, the rubric and the lecturer's short notes per rubric item.
loop.output: Draft feedback comments per rubric item, each quoting the passage it refers to.
loop.check: Code drops any comment whose quoted passage is not in the paper; the lecturer edits every comment; no score is proposed.
loop.stop: One draft per paper; stop when a rubric item lacks a quoted passage and leave that item to the lecturer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments must refer to each student's own text; fixed comment banks read as generic.

steps.what: Lecturer decides the grade for each paper
Lecturer enters grades in the learning system and again in the student records system

tasks.design: Code in the learning system ({LMS}) checks length, citation format and whether references resolve, so the lecturer does not check these by hand. From the lecturer's short notes per rubric item, a bounded step drafts feedback comments that quote the paper; comments whose quote is not in the paper are dropped, and the lecturer edits every comment. No score is proposed: the lecturer decides every grade. Grades are entered once and sync to the student records system instead of being typed twice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Form checks were done by hand, every comment typed in full and grades entered twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems draft feedback from instructor notes; grade sync is standard.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can praise or fault passages generically.
tasks.human_edge: Judging an original argument that breaks the rubric's mould.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer edits feedback and decides grades instead of typing every comment.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.

At the University of Michigan, assistants edited FeedbackWriter's rubric suggestions for 1,366 essays from 354 students, agreed with 88% of its judgements, and revisions were significantly better; no time data.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk; duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from papers submitted to grades entered; appeals are outside.
Input contract: rubric per assignment; fallback is writing comments in full.
The lecturer decides every grade; the tool proposes no scores.
A DPIA and the examination board's consent come before use.
s5 is part of keeping grade records, which sibling task 25-1123.00:6314 covers; its saving is counted there, so s5 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: How much of each drafted comment does the lecturer keep?

incremental.description: Lecturer compares a sample of drafted comments with own reading each term.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short papers with few comments; high: long papers in large groups.

tasks.short: Update the syllabus with dates, rooms and readings, write homework assignments, make handouts, check the materials, and publish them in the learning system.

steps.what: Lecturer updates the syllabus with dates, rooms and readings by hand

loop.input: The learning outcomes, the week's readings and earlier assignments.
loop.output: Draft assignment texts with instructions and a rubric outline.
loop.check: Any reading or reference in the draft must resolve to the course list, a DOI or the library catalogue, else it is dropped; the lecturer edits every assignment.
loop.stop: One draft per assignment; if rejected, the lecturer writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each assignment must fit the week's readings; a template gives only the frame.

steps.what: Lecturer checks the final course materials
Lecturer uploads the materials to the learning system for students

tasks.design: The syllabus is generated from the course catalogue entry, the timetable and the reading list ({LMS}), so dates, rooms and readings are not typed by hand. A bounded step drafts homework assignments from the learning outcomes and the week's readings; references that do not resolve are dropped, and the lecturer edits every assignment. Handouts are kept in a tagged material bank and reused. Once checked, materials are released to students on set dates from the learning system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Syllabi were retyped each term and assignments written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems generate schedules; university chat platforms draft teaching texts.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the text that will start a real argument in class.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer edits and selects instead of retyping.

evidence.claim: EduGenAI is a university chat platform in pilot for teachers; Utrecht forbids automated grading on it.
Plagiarism checks do not flag invented references.
Drafting course materials is not a high-risk use under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course term to materials published; course design is outside.
Input contract: timetable and reading list in the learning system; fallback is typing.
The lecturer checks every item before release.
research_questions: How much of each drafted assignment is kept?

approvals.approved_version: The materials as checked by the lecturer in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new courses; high: repeated courses with set readings.

tasks.short: Prepare discussion questions, moderate classroom discussions, and note participation on a paper list that is typed in later.

steps.what: Lecturer prepares questions to initiate classroom discussions
Lecturer facilitates and moderates classroom discussions
Lecturer notes participation on a paper list and types it in later

tasks.design: Participation is marked on the class list in the learning system ({LMS}) on a tablet during or right after class, so it is not written on paper and typed in later. Preparing questions and moderating discussions stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Participation was noted on paper and typed in later.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold class lists for marking on a tablet.
tasks.still_hard: Marking during a lively discussion distracts.
tasks.human_edge: Drawing a quiet student into the discussion.

reach.learn: Whether participation marks are visible sooner.

evidence.claim: Learning systems hold class lists that can be marked on a tablet.
Emotion inference in education is banned.

assumptions: Boundary: from the class scheduled to participation recorded; grading is outside.
Input contract: class lists in the learning system; fallback is paper.
research_questions: Is participation recorded the same day more often?

incremental.description: Lecturer corrects marks entered in a hurry.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small classes; high: large seminar groups.
